newsitem.title: USA: Terra Industries Q1 hurt by late planting.
newsitem.headline: Terra Industries Q1 hurt by late planting.

text.p: Terra Industries Inc said Tuesday its earnings for the first quarter were hurt by increased natural gas costs and a slow start to the spring planting season.

Earlier, it reported net income of $3.9 million, or $0.05 a share, on revenues of $433.7 million for the first quarter. That compared with year-ago net income of $18.4 million, or $0.23 per share, on revenues of $394.7 million.

Nitrogen products revenue in the quarter fell to $135.9 million from $153.1 million, while methanol revenue rose to $43.0 million from $28.9 million. Distribution revenue rose to $260.5 million from $222.9 million.

"Weather has had a significant effect this year," Burton Joyce, Terra president, said in a statement. "Very cold winter temperatures caused gas prices to reach extraordinarily high levels. Wet conditions in the South delayed the start of field activity there. And the melting of record snowfalls in the northern part of the country will result in a late planting season in some areas of the Cornbelt."
He added that the company is optimistic that more favorable weather will result in "a great deal of catch-up acitivity" in the fields.
"Much of the lost first quarter revenue could be made up in the second and third quarter," he said.
Terra markets and produces fertilizer, crop protection products, seed and services.
